reasons: Lake identity gives case_name_full as Scott v. Harris, court as U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided as 2007-04-30, and year as 2007.
Lake citations list official cite 550 U.S. 372, parallel cites 127 S. Ct. 1769 and 167 L. Ed. 2d 686, and vendor-neutral cite 2007 U.S. LEXIS 4748.
The opinion states that excessive-force seizure claims are analyzed under the Fourth Amendment's objective-reasonableness standard and asks whether Scott's actions were objectively reasonable.

The opinion rejects Garner as rigid deadly-force preconditions: "Garner did not establish a magical on/off switch" and "Garner was simply an application of the Fourth Amendment's reasonableness test" as tied to Graham.

The opinion concludes that the chase posed a substantial and immediate risk of serious physical injury to others and that Scott's attempt to terminate it by forcing Harris off the road was reasonable.
residual_risks: The holding would be more precise if limited to a dangerous high-speed chase threatening innocent bystanders, rather than the shorter phrase "fleeing motorist who endangered the public."
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Replace the last clause with: "forcing a fleeing motorist off the road during a dangerous high-speed chase threatening innocent bystanders was reasonable."
